title: budget.spent
description: A resource was consumed by one run: a pi run (researcher, lab assistant, admin chat) or a verifier run. Who spent it is in the envelope `actor`; what it was spent on is the envelope `cause` (the job, visit or check it served). The substrate REPORTS spend; caps are loop policy. Subject is pool:<name>.

pool.description: Which resource pool was drawn from: 'claude' (the human's Pro plan, shared with their own use; no published quota), 'qwen' (self-hosted on the DGX Spark, free but bounded by decode throughput), 'cpu' (the devbox's 16 cores, used by verification). Free string so pools can be added. Subject is pool:<pool>.

tokens_in.description: Prompt tokens. Zero for non-model work such as the cpu pool. Count UNCACHED and cached together here; record the cached portion separately in tokens_cached.

tokens_out.description: Completion tokens. For the qwen pool this is the real constraint — aggregate output throughput, not context or request count, is what bounds how many lab assistants can run.

tokens_cached.description: Portion of tokens_in served from a prompt cache. Worth tracking: the standing brief is a stable prefix, so with consults inside the cache TTL the fixed context costs roughly a tenth of list price. Big enough to change allocation decisions.

cpu_seconds.description: Core-seconds consumed, for cpu-pool work such as verification. Reveals whether verification or generation is the real bottleneck.

wall_seconds.description: Elapsed time of the run. With tokens_out it gives per-run throughput, and shows where time goes.

usd.description: Actual or imputed dollar cost. Null for subscription and local usage. Impute a notional value anyway where you can — it is the only way to compare a free local pool against a metered one.
